operator_request: Remediate every finding from the completed product-code versus completed-work-packet spot check, then commit, push, and provide an overview of remaining work.

research_reopen_triggers: The Operator explicitly requests new research.
The pinned Serde behavior, Rust toolchain, dependency set, or architecture harness assumption is proven stale.
A remediation decision lacks evidence in the technical design, WP-005, WP-013, archived WP-014 v1, current source, or reproduced public-boundary behavior.
existing_research_sources: WP-013 official Rust and Serde implementation research
WP-013 strict Serde DTO, public-boundary counterexample, and isolated-mutation patterns
Current storage contract, testkit, architecture fixtures, rule mapping, and gate implementation
Direct public deserialization reproductions and v1 focused, workspace, architecture, and deep proof
selected_approach: Preserve the complete v1 technical remediation and proof.
Archive v1 with its two truthful runtime failures instead of backfilling its activation.
Activate v2 with the exact machine-readable non-product prerequisite declaration present from the first committed checkpoint.
Rerun runtime-truth and PR validation against v2, then complete adversarial closure.
rejected_options: Rewriting or amending v1 activation history.
Treating a late v1 declaration as equivalent to predeclaration.
Discarding the already verified contract and mutation work.
Adding dependencies, changing valid wire shape, or creating a parallel proof framework.
reuse_opportunities: Reuse every v1 contract change, test, fixture, report, and failure record.
Reuse the validated WP-013 supersession pattern.
Reuse runtime-truth's activation checkpoint proof to validate v2 independently.
basis.validation_plan: Commit v2 with the prerequisite object already present, rerun runtime-truth and PR gates from the v2 taskboard focus, independently inspect the full base-to-head diff and boundary behavior, record all findings and residual uncertainty, then execute closure and main-containment proof.

assumptions: The existing locked Serde dependency and Rust toolchain remain current.
The current journal JSON shape is authoritative for compatibility.
No shipped Ferric archive/journal runtime consumer exists.
The v1 product and proof commits remain within the preserved v2 base-to-head scope.
non_goals: Changing valid durable-wire tags or field names.
Creating a shipped runtime or advancing product phase state.
Erasing v1 activation defects or failure reports.

minimum_controls: Each invalid case is tested through public serde_json deserialization.
Canonical valid records decode and serialize to the same JSON value.
Constructed records have an explicit invariant-validation method.
Each corrected guard has a distinct isolated mutation fixture and marker.
The canonical architecture gate executes all mapped fixtures.
Runtime-truth proves the v2 prerequisite declaration existed at first commit.
plausible_failures: Undeclared variant data is silently ignored.
A zero sequence breaks durable ordering or replay.
A future refactor removes one guard while the architecture gate remains green.
A mutation runs zero tests or fails for an unrelated reason.
A late packet edit is presented as an activation-time declaration.

execution_decomposition: Commit this v2 activation checkpoint with the structured prerequisite declaration.
Rerun runtime-truth and PR validation from the active v2 packet.
Complete the independent adversarial diff review and packet evidence.
Commit closure, merge to main, verify containment, push, and report remaining authoritative work.
